name: Rendak Mango-Habanero Fruit Leathers
description: Hand-rolled synth-fruit leathers pressed with real dried habanero flake and a mango-forward base that builds slow heat. Sold in folded wax-paper sleeves from Tier 1 kiosks up to Tier 3 corner shops.
flavor_profile: Sweet mango up front, then a slow-building habanero burn that lingers on the back of the throat; slightly chewy with a sticky finish
cultural_context: A Shelf staple passed down through food-cart lineages; Rendak is a family-run operation with three generations of recipes encoded in their synth-fruit formula, and locals take pride in knowing which cart has the 'original' batch.
story_hooks: A Rendak cart operator is threatened by a Tier 4 corponation attempting to buy out the recipe IP and mass-produce a sanitized version — the family must decide whether to sell or fight.
A Tier 5 food critic goes viral after posting about Rendak leathers, flooding Shelf markets with tourists and disrupting the local economy.
The habanero flake supplier suddenly goes dark, and a runner is hired to find out why the supply chain vanished overnight.
